title: Redwood All-Hands - March 2026
summary: Quarterly all-hands covering Q1 milestones: Dedicated capacity growth, Private product beta, reliability incidents and remediation, hiring updates, and company metrics. Leadership Q&A and action items for Security docs and customer success playbook.
action_items: Jordan Lee: publish reliability postmortem draft to ops-docs; due 2026-03-19
Priya Nair: share Private beta runbook and checklist; due 2026-03-18
Samir Desai: circulate updated roadmap deck for sales enablement; due 2026-03-16
Maya Chen: schedule follow-up on KV cache perf benchmarks with SE team; due 2026-03-20
next_steps: Leadership to send annotated deck and key metrics by EOD
Engineering to complete reliability action items and share timeline
Customer Success to coordinate Private beta invites and NDA workflows
All: submit questions for town-hall follow-up in #all-hands-questions channel
transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-03-12
Start: 10:00 AM PT
Duration: ~58 minutes
Attendees: Elliot Ramos, Maya Chen, Samir Desai, Jordan Lee, Priya Nair, plus company-wide listeners

[00:00] Elliot: Alright, hi everyone, welcome to the March all-hands. Uh, thanks for joining on time, we've got a fairly full agenda today, I'll run through the top-line business updates, then Maya and Priya will walk through engineering and research updates, Samir will do product/GT R stuff and then we'll open it up for Q&A.

[00:34] Elliot: Quick note, for folks in EMEA/APAC, we recorded this and we'll post the deck in the channel. Also, if you have any sensitive questions, please drop them in the anonymous form, we'll try to cover them.

[01:10] Elliot: High level — Q1 performance. Revenue is up 28% quarter over quarter, go-to-market is seeing consistent usage increases across hosted API and Dedicated trials. Biggest wave is Dedicated commits from two larger customers, both on multi-month pilots. Cost per token trends continue to improve thanks to batching and some kernel-level ops from the runtime team.

[02:05] Audience (murmur)

[02:22] Elliot: We're still seeing margin pressure in some workloads, especially small request volume with low batching efficiency, and of course Private deployments have a higher fixed op cost but bring bigger ARR. Overall, I think we're in a good shape to hit our Q2 commitments.

[03:10] Maya: Hey, quick engineering update. On Dedicated we shipped autoscaling improvements — this reduces cold-start latency for small bursts by about 40% in internal tests. The team also completed an initial KV cache eviction policy change that should help long-context workloads. There's still work to be done for memory usage with quantized big models.

[04:05] Elliot: Can you unpack the KV change a bit?

[04:10] Maya: Sure — previously eviction was time-based windowing; we moved to a usage-weighted LR-inspired policy so hot prefixes stay cached. In our benchmarks the 2k-4k seq workloads saw a median latency drop of 12-15%. Caveat — transcription: some of the perf numbers were from lab runs not all customer traffic, so ymmv.

[05:02] Priya: From Research: we launched an internal eval harness for regression detection — it's catching quality regressions earlier. We've started tagging regressions to model variants and quantization profiles. Also trialing a compact LLM variant that reduces memory by ~30% with small quality tradeoffs. We'll share more in the private alpha notes.

[05:50] Elliot: Nice. Quick call-out on Private — we've onboarded 3 beta customers and are working through network setups. Jordan can expand on the onboarding bottlenecks.

[06:18] Jordan: Onboarding summary: the major friction is customer-side networking (firewall rules, KMS policy setup) and the audit log retention config. We've put together a checklist and a one-page runbook; Priya will share the runbook. Also want to reduce the number of manual handoffs — automation of the VPC peering and cert provisioning is Q2 priority.

[07:10] Audience member: Is there an ETA for automating cert provisioning?

[07:16] Jordan: We're targeting mid-April for an MVP and full automation by the end of Q2, contingent on a small infra hiring slot.

[07:42] Samir: Product-wise: roadmap highlights — 1) improved streaming semantics and partial-output commits, 2) function/tool calling enhancements for structured outputs, 3) embeddings dedupe/cache layer for similarity workloads. For sales, we'll produce a short playbook outlining when to recommend Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private.

[08:25] Elliot: On the point of Hosted vs Dedicated, something we've heard a lot from customers is the cost vs latency tradeoff. We need clearer guidance and examples — Samir, prioritize a decision-tree doc for AEs.

[08:40] Samir: Yep, will do.

[09:05] Elliot: Now, reliability — we had a notable incident two weeks ago impacting a subset of Dedicated pools. Jordan, can you do the postmortem recap?

[09:18] Jordan: Sure. Root cause: autoscaler misconfiguration + a rollout of a new kernel selection policy that caused increased memory fragmentation on a particular driver/hardware combo. The autoscaler reacted by spinning up new nodes but the fragmentation persisted, leading to evictions and increased tail latency. Mitigations applied: rollback of kernel policy, immediate patch to the autoscaler to throttle scale-up, and emergency eviction tuning. We're doing deeper fixes: better kernel-driver compatibility tests, and a pre-rollout canary for kernel policy changes.

[10:40] Audience: Were customers notified?

[10:48] Jordan: Yes — CS sent incident notifications and targeted apologies. We also offered credits to affected accounts and gave a technical postmortem to customers who asked.

[11:15] Elliot: Thanks Jordan. Two important takeaways: one, we need better automated detection of fragmentation patterns; two, let's make the playbook for incident comms more prescriptive for SEs and CSMs. Action for Jordan to publish the internal postmortem draft by next week.

[12:02] Maya: Hiring update — we've filled three backend infra roles and two more in model infra. Open priorities: infra reliability engineer, security infra engineer, and a senior ML infra engineer. Please refer to the #hiring channel for referrals.

[12:38] Elliot: Compensation and promotions — small note: we're finalizing the promotion cycle this month, managers will share outcomes privately.

[13:05] Priya: Research hiring — we have two offers out for applied researchers focusing on quantization-aware training and eval automation; that should accelerate the quantized model variant work.

[13:40] Samir: GTM — enterprise deals: we closed a mid-market account in EU with Dedicated commit and an initial Private pilot. This is a nice validation for the private product. Also pipeline looks healthy for Q2 with several RFPs in the legal stage.

[14:12] Audience member (question): Any update on compliance certifications? SOC 2?

[14:20] Elliot: We're on track with SOC 2 Type I material proofs and gearing for Type II next year. Security has the roadmap for ISO and other audits; exact timelines depend on resource allocation.

[14:45] Jordan: Also want to highlight ongoing work on audit logs and longer retention options for enterprise customers — that'll be configurable in Private and Dedicated in Q3.

[15:10] Elliot: Ok next I want to cover compensation of time and where to focus — product-market fit signals: Dedicated commit velocity, churn on hosted free tier, and Private beta conversion. If those numbers trend favorably, we scale dedicated capacity and sales motion for enterprise.

[15:46] Elliot: Quick metrics — activation time for Dedicated trials down from 9 days to 6 days, DSATs on onboarding reduced by 18% after we added the runbook. Net dollar retention in pilot cohort is at 1.12, a little noisy but encouraging.

[16:30] Priya: Short research note — we're putting together a short internal doc on regression tolerance thresholds per customer segment; the idea is to tie model variant choices to customer SLAs.

[17:05] Audience: Question about the compact LLM variant — any expected perf regressions?

[17:12] Priya: Early tests show slight drop in instruction-following on edge cases; overall quality delta is around 2-4% on our automated metrics. We'll push a formal comparison for customers considering cost-first profiles.

[17:45] Elliot: Alright, let's do Q&A. Please keep questions short — and state your name/team.

[18:05] Speaker (Jules, Sales): Thanks. Two quick asks — 1) a one-pager on security guarantees for Private to share with prospects, 2) an RD on when to recommend quantization rules for customers.

[18:22] Elliot: Action: Security one-pager — Jordan and Security team to deliver; Priya to add model-related guidance.

[18:38] Speaker (Tara, CSM): On incident credits — can we standardize the threshold for credits vs advisory support? A lot of manual decisions now.

[18:48] Jordan: We'll propose a standard tiered policy and share with CSMs.

[19:05] Speaker (Dev Team): Quick technical — are we tracking KV cache hit-rate per tenant anywhere?

[19:12] Maya: Yes, we have metrics but not surfaced in the console per-tenant yet. That's an RFE. We'll add it to the observability backlog.

[19:35] Elliot: Time check — about 40 minutes left — ok keep them coming.

[20:02] Speaker (Ben, Support): If Private customers want on-prem, what's our stance on air-gapped installs?

[20:12] Jordan: We have an on-prem package; air-gapped installs are supported on a case-by-case basis and involve longer lead times and legal review. We'll document the standard timeline.

[20:40] Speaker (Ana, Marketing): Any wins to share for content?

[20:45] Samir: We released two benchmark blog posts and a case study; marketing will circulate the links.

[21:10] Audience (multiple): applause

[21:45] Elliot: Closing remarks — we're making steady progress on reliability and product breadth. Please keep focus on shipping the Private runbook automation and the incident postmortem. Thanks for the questions and the energy. We'll follow up with the deck and notes.

[22:05] Elliot: End of meeting.

Note: transcription contains occasional speaker label drift and some words may be slightly off; timestamps approximate.
